W1 (mechanism), after E021.

**Setup.** The tip is E017 (E016 math, break-free): Muon on renormalized conv filters (so filter wd is inert, and Newton-Schulz runs 3 steps); SGD on BN biases, whitening bias and head at wd 0.006; Lookahead/EMA every 5 steps; 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps; batch 2000; 238 steps (about 9.5 true epochs); widths 128/384/512; max-autotune with CUDA graphs. Score: 6.548 s, 0.7537.

**Noise**
- Rebuilding the same commit moves the 3-seed mean by about 0.04 pp (E017 vs E019).
- A code-path change reshuffles per-seed trajectories by about ±0.2-0.35 pp on the 3-seed mean (E016 0.7607 vs E017 0.7537, same math).
- True tip mean: about 0.7545-0.755.
- Hypotheses whose bar is "relative to E016 (0.7607)" carry about −0.5 pp of built-in bias, and nearly all fail on that alone.

**Time model (revised by E021)**
- Changes to steps and resolution scale time almost 1:1 (E020: −10.5% steps gave −10.5% time; E018: −8% MACs gave −8.5% time).
- Width cuts do not: E021 removed 15.6% of MACs but saved only 7.8% of time. At the narrower width the kernels run at lower tensor-core efficiency, or the group-2 convs were already under-utilizing the GPU, so time per MAC rises.
- Expect architecture cuts to return about 50-60% of their MAC fraction as time. Dropping group-1 conv3 (6.5% of MACs, at the largest maps, with memory-bound BN/GELU) should give about −4 to −6%.

**Accuracy exchange rates (pp lost per 10% of time saved, against a true baseline of about 0.755)**
- Epochs: about 0.25 pp (E020: −10.5% time, 0.7528).
- Group-2 width: about 0.25-0.3 pp (E021: −7.8%, 0.7530). This is cheaper than I predicted, so width and epochs are now about equally priced at roughly 2.5-3 s per pp.
- Last-group width: about 0.45 pp (E010).
- Resolution, early phase: about 0.8-1.2 pp (E011, E018). The low-resolution phases do real feature learning, and the 28 px bridge matters.

**Measured mechanisms**
- Lookahead/EMA: +1 pp (E005).
- Muon: +0.5 ± 0.3 pp (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −20% time for −0.5 pp (E007).
- Flat within noise: LS 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5, LR floor 0, wd ×0.5. The regularization knobs are insensitive, so a further SGD-group wd cut should also be flat.

**Strategy**
- The true margin is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Every single lever measured so far (−1 epoch, group 2 at 320, 24/32 swap) lands at about 0.750-0.753, just under the line.
- The feasible next moves are smaller steps on the cheapest dials:
  - a −0.5 epoch trim (about −5% time, about −0.12 pp);
  - group 2 at 352;
  - a combination of a mild width cut with a +0.25 epoch top-up only if it is net time-negative.
- Seed luck decides 3-seed feasibility within ±0.25 pp. Each attempt near the line is roughly a coin flip.
- No booster worth 0.3 pp or more is in hand. BN recalibration and a stronger EMA are the remaining untested ideas.

**Unsure**
- The 10-seed true mean of the tip.
- Why 320 lost efficiency (tile shape or under-utilization), and whether 352 or 384-wide variants of other groups behave the same way.
- Whether a booster above 0.3 pp exists.
- PCIe transfer of accuracy.

forecasts.reason: Regularization knobs are flat on this recipe, and the bar of +0.2 pp over E016's lucky 0.7607 needs about 0.763, which is far above the true mean of about 0.755.
6.5% of MACs returns only about 5% of time (the E021 efficiency loss), short of the 8% bar, and the 0.4 pp bar against 0.7607 is also likely missed.
Resolution costs about 1 pp per 10% of time; −3.4% time for about −0.3 pp, which misses both the 4% time bar and the bar of 0.7582 (0.25 pp below E016).

cruxes: What is the tip's true 10-seed mean (0.7545 or 0.757)? This decides whether −0.5 epoch or a mild width cut can clear 0.753 reliably.
Why did group 2 at 320 return only half its MAC savings as time (kernel tile efficiency or under-utilization)? This sets the payoff of every architectural lever.
Does any time-neutral booster (BN recalibration after the EMA swap, a stronger or longer EMA) add 0.3 pp or more to fund the trims?
